What is a Preliminary Cost Estimate and Why Does It Matter?
Gain Valuable Insights with Conceptual Estimates and Project Feasibility
A Preliminary estimate is an approximate cost calculated during the conceptual stage of a project. It helps stakeholders like builders, owners, contractors, and real estate developers get a general idea of how much the project will likely cost. Preliminary or conceptual estimates are commonly used in construction project management and financial planning to provide an early understanding of the potential costs, resources, or outcomes associated with a particular endeavor.
Since the project drawings and specifications are still in their early stages, the preliminary estimate is an initial assessment based on limited information. It allows for early decision-making and helps determine the feasibility and viability of the project.
Types of Preliminary Estimates for Different Project Stages
There are several methods and tools available to calculate a preliminary estimate. These may include using historical data from similar projects, applying unit rates, utilizing cost databases, or employing conceptual estimating software. We tailor our approach to match the extent of available information and deliver assessments with the desired accuracy.
Rough Order Magnitude (ROM) Estimate: At the early stages of your project, our ROM estimates provide a broad range of costs, allowing you to analyze the feasibility and make high-level decisions. With an accuracy range of -50% to +50%, these estimates serve as a valuable starting point.
Ballpark Estimate: When you need to define the project’s scope within your client’s budget, Ballpark estimates come into play. Based on preliminary drawings and specifications, these estimates offer a closer approximation with an accuracy range of around 20% of the actual cost.
Budget Estimate: As your project progresses into the planning stage, our budget estimates utilize past project data and plans to provide detailed cost breakdowns. With an accuracy range of -10% to +25%, these estimates assist in allocating funds and establishing cost limits.
Definitive Estimate: When your project reaches the advanced planning phase, our definitive estimates offer detailed itemized lists of the components involved. Utilizing thoroughly developed project plans, these estimates provide enhanced accuracy, typically falling within a range of -5% to +15%.
